files.README.md:
# django-postgresql-conversions-import

Data access layer generated by [DB2CRUD](https://github.com/RaulEstevezA/DB2CRUD) for a database that already exists: entities, repositories and services with the Django 5.2 ORM. It does not create or migrate the database.

## Settings

- Database: postgresql; code: synchronous (Session).
- Entities: written for the tables the input had no class for.
- Services: take and return DTOs (pydantic).
- Transactions: one transaction per service operation, committed when it ends.
- Lists: lists return pages by offset and limit.

## Layout

```text
app/settings.py        Django settings: the database comes from DATABASE_URL
app/models.py          imports every entity, for Django's app registry
app/errors.py          NotFoundError, ConflictError, ValidationFailedError: no HTTP codes
app/unit_of_work.py    the repositories of every table, and the transaction of each operation
app/entities/          one entity per table
app/repositories/      one repository per table
app/services/          one service per table
tests/                 repositories against a database, services on the in-memory repositories
crud-contract.json     what was written, for CRUD2Controller
```

## Running the tests

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest                       # SQLite in a temporary file
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://app:app@localhost:5432/app python -m pytest   # a real, disposable database: it is emptied
```

"""Conversions between the application models and the "products" table: what the service takes and returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

from app.application_models import Product as ProductModel
from app.dtos.product import ProductCreate, ProductRead
from app.errors import NotFoundError
from app.unit_of_work import UnitOfWork


def product_model_to_product_create(model: ProductModel, uow: UnitOfWork) -> ProductCreate:
    """A Product as the products table takes it."""
    category = uow.categories.find_by_name(model.category_name)
    if category is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Category", model.category_name)
    return ProductCreate(
        category_id=category.id,
        name=model.name,
        price=model.price,
        status=model.status,
    )


def product_read_to_product_model(row: ProductRead, uow: UnitOfWork) -> ProductModel:
    """A row of the products table as a Product."""
    category = uow.categories.find_by_id(row.category_id)
    return ProductModel(
        id=row.id,
        name=row.name,
        price=row.price,
        status=row.status,
        category_name=category.name if category is not None else None,
        tag_ids=[item.tag_id for item in uow.product_tags.list_by_product_id(row.id)],
    )

"""Django settings of the data access layer: only what the ORM needs. The database comes from DATABASE_URL;
see .env.example. Import this module from your project's settings, or point DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE to it."""

import os
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit


def database_from_url(url: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A Django database from a URL: postgresql://user:password@host:port/name, mysql://…, sqlite:///path or
    sqlite://:memory:. A driver after the scheme (postgresql+psycopg) is ignored."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    scheme = parts.scheme.split("+", 1)[0]
    if scheme == "sqlite":
        return {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": parts.netloc or parts.path[1:] or ":memory:"}
    engine = {"postgresql": "postgresql", "postgres": "postgresql", "mysql": "mysql", "mariadb": "mysql"}[scheme]
    if engine == "mysql":
        # PyMySQL stands in for mysqlclient, which needs a C compiler and the MySQL client library
        import pymysql

        pymysql.install_as_MySQLdb()
    return {
        "ENGINE": f"django.db.backends.{engine}",
        "NAME": parts.path.lstrip("/"),
        "USER": unquote(parts.username or ""),
        "PASSWORD": unquote(parts.password or ""),
        "HOST": parts.hostname or "",
        "PORT": str(parts.port or ""),
    }


SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("DJANGO_SECRET_KEY", "only-the-orm-is-used-change-it-in-your-project")
INSTALLED_APPS = ["app"]
DATABASES = {"default": database_from_url(os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://app:app@localhost:5432/app"))}
USE_TZ = True
TIME_ZONE = "UTC"
DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD = "django.db.models.BigAutoField"

"""The repositories of every table, and the transaction of each service operation. Each service operation runs in `transaction()`: committed when it ends, rolled back when it fails."""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import AbstractContextManager, contextmanager
from typing import Protocol

from django.db import transaction

from app.repositories.category import CategoryRepository, MemoryCategoryRepository, SqlCategoryRepository
from app.repositories.customer import CustomerRepository, MemoryCustomerRepository, SqlCustomerRepository
from app.repositories.product import MemoryProductRepository, ProductRepository, SqlProductRepository
from app.repositories.product_tag import MemoryProductTagRepository, ProductTagRepository, SqlProductTagRepository
from app.repositories.tag import MemoryTagRepository, SqlTagRepository, TagRepository


class UnitOfWork(Protocol):
    """What services depend on: a repository per table and a transaction."""

    customers: CustomerRepository
    categories: CategoryRepository
    products: ProductRepository
    tags: TagRepository
    product_tags: ProductTagRepository

    def transaction(self) -> AbstractContextManager[None]:
        """Commits what runs inside it, or rolls it back if it fails."""
        ...


class SqlUnitOfWork:
    """The repositories over the Django database connection."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.customers = SqlCustomerRepository()
        self.categories = SqlCategoryRepository()
        self.products = SqlProductRepository()
        self.tags = SqlTagRepository()
        self.product_tags = SqlProductTagRepository()

    @contextmanager
    def transaction(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """Commits what runs inside it, or rolls it back if it fails (transaction.atomic)."""
        with transaction.atomic():
            yield


class MemoryUnitOfWork:
    """The in-memory repositories, for tests and for trying the services without a database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.customers = MemoryCustomerRepository()
        self.categories = MemoryCategoryRepository()
        self.products = MemoryProductRepository()
        self.tags = MemoryTagRepository()
        self.product_tags = MemoryProductTagRepository()

    @contextmanager
    def transaction(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """Memory has no transactions: changes are kept as they are made."""
        yield

"""Tests of the "categories" table."""

from dataclasses import fields

import pytest
from tests.factories import add_category, new_category

from app.dtos.category import CategoryCreate, CategoryUpdate
from app.errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
from app.services.category import CategoryService
from app.unit_of_work import MemoryUnitOfWork, SqlUnitOfWork


def test_category_is_stored_and_read_back(sql_uow: SqlUnitOfWork) -> None:
    stored = add_category(sql_uow, 1)
    found = sql_uow.categories.find_by_id(stored.id)
    assert found is not None
    assert found.id == stored.id
    assert sql_uow.categories.find_by_name(stored.name) is not None


def test_category_lists_rows_by_key(sql_uow: SqlUnitOfWork) -> None:
    add_category(sql_uow, 1)
    add_category(sql_uow, 2)
    page = sql_uow.categories.list(0, 1)
    assert page.total == 2
    assert len(page.items) == 1


def test_category_is_deleted(sql_uow: SqlUnitOfWork) -> None:
    stored = add_category(sql_uow, 1)
    sql_uow.categories.delete(stored)
    assert sql_uow.categories.find_by_id(stored.id) is None


def test_category_service_creates_a_valid_row(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    n = 100
    created = service.create_category(CategoryCreate(**_values(new_category(1), CategoryCreate)))
    found = service.get_category(created.id)
    assert found.id == created.id


def test_category_service_refuses_a_missing_value(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    n = 100
    with pytest.raises(ValidationFailedError) as raised:
        service.create_category(CategoryCreate.model_construct(**(_values(new_category(1), CategoryCreate) | {"name": None})))
    assert [error.field for error in raised.value.errors] == ["name"]


def test_category_service_refuses_a_repeated_unique_value(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    n = 100
    first = service.create_category(CategoryCreate(**_values(new_category(1), CategoryCreate)))
    with pytest.raises(ConflictError):
        service.create_category(CategoryCreate(**_values(new_category(2, name=first.name), CategoryCreate)))


def test_category_service_keeps_its_own_unique_value(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    n = 100
    created = service.create_category(CategoryCreate(**_values(new_category(1), CategoryCreate)))
    service.update_category(created.id, CategoryUpdate(name=created.name))


def test_category_service_says_when_a_row_is_missing(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    with pytest.raises(NotFoundError):
        service.get_category(999999)


def test_category_service_deletes_a_row(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    service = CategoryService(memory_uow)
    n = 100
    created = service.create_category(CategoryCreate(**_values(new_category(1), CategoryCreate)))
    service.delete_category(created.id)
    with pytest.raises(NotFoundError):
        service.get_category(created.id)


def _values(entity: object, dto: type) -> dict[str, object]:
    """The values a DTO takes, from an entity that is not stored, for building the DTO from a factory row."""
    names = dto.model_fields if hasattr(dto, "model_fields") else {field.name for field in fields(dto)}
    return {name: value for name, value in vars(entity).items() if name in names}

"""Tests of the conversions between the application models and the tables."""

from tests.factories import add_category, add_product

from app.conversions.category import category_dto_to_category_create, category_read_to_category_dto
from app.conversions.product import product_model_to_product_create, product_read_to_product_model
from app.unit_of_work import MemoryUnitOfWork


def test_category_dto_goes_both_ways(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    """A row read as a CategoryDto and written back gives the same values."""
    row = add_category(memory_uow)
    model = category_read_to_category_dto(row)
    assert model.id == row.id
    assert model.name == row.name
    values = category_dto_to_category_create(model)
    assert values.name == row.name


def test_product_goes_both_ways(memory_uow: MemoryUnitOfWork) -> None:
    """A row read as a Product and written back gives the same values."""
    row = add_product(memory_uow)
    model = product_read_to_product_model(row, memory_uow)
    assert model.id == row.id
    assert model.name == row.name
    assert model.price == row.price
    assert model.status == row.status
    values = product_model_to_product_create(model, memory_uow)
    assert values.category_id == row.category_id
    assert values.name == row.name
    assert values.price == row.price
    assert values.status == row.status

"""The tests run on the database they were asked to."""

import os

from django.db import connection


def test_runs_on_the_database_asked(db) -> None:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    url = os.environ.get("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
    expected = url.split(":", 1)[0].split("+", 1)[0] if url else "sqlite"
    # Django runs MariaDB with its MySQL backend
    assert connection.vendor == ("mysql" if expected == "mariadb" else expected)
